questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The philanthropist's ________ donations significantly improved the quality of life in the community.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**substantial**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**substantial**" means of considerable importance, size, or worth. (महत्वपूर्ण, बड़ा, या मूल्यवान)
 
• The philanthropist's substantial donations indicate that the contributions were significant and impactful in improving the community's quality of life.
 
• The other options: "**meagre**," "**parsimonious**," and "**redundant**" do not fit the context as appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The philanthropist's substantial__ donations significantly improved the quality of life in the community.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Meagre (अल्प)**: means lacking in quantity or quality.
 
• **Parsimonious (कंजूस)**: means very unwilling to spend money or use resources.
 
• **Redundant (अतिरिक्त)**: means not or no longer needed or useful.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Following weeks of intense training, the athlete _______________ in the championship.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**competed**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "**competed**" is the simple past tense form of the verb "**compete**."
 
• The sentence describes an action that occurred in the past ("**Following weeks of intense training**"), so the past tense "**competed**" is required.
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and **4 **are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Following weeks of intense training, the athlete **competed**__ in the championship."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "were competing"** is incorrect because it is in the past continuous tense, which is not appropriate for this context.
 
• **Option 2: "have been competing"** is incorrect because it is in the present perfect continuous tense, which is not suitable for a completed past action.
 
• **Option 4: "have competed"** is incorrect because it is in the present perfect tense, which is not appropriate for this context.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.

These are the works of a great poet Tagore.

options.text: These are the works of that great poet Tagore.
These are the works of an great poet Tagore.
These are the works of this great poet Tagore.
These are the works of the great poet Tagore.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires the use of the definite article "**the**" before the phrase "great poet Tagore" to specify and emphasize that it is referring to a particular poet, Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• The use of "**an**" in Option 2 is incorrect because "great" begins with a consonant sound, not a vowel sound.
 
• Option 1 and Option 3, while grammatically correct, use "that" and "this" which are not necessary and make the sentence less natural in this context.
 
• Option 4, "**These are the works of the great poet Tagore**," is grammatically correct and clear in its structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "These are the works of that great poet Tagore" – While this is grammatically correct, the use of "that" makes it less formal and less appropriate.
 
• **Option 2:** "These are the works of an great poet Tagore" – This is incorrect because "an" cannot be used before a word starting with a consonant sound like "great."
 
• **Option 3:** "These are the works of this great poet Tagore" – While correct, "this" adds unnecessary specificity, which is not needed in the given context.

questions.question:
Select the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence.

The state played only a __modest__ part in the outstanding advancement of modern morality.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Boastful**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"modest"** means someone or something that is humble, unassuming, or moderate in estimation of one’s abilities or achievements. (विनम्र, मामूली)

 
 
• **Example: **She gave a modest reply when congratulated on her success.
 
 
 
• **"Boastful" **refers to someone who talks with excessive pride about their achievements, possessions, or abilities. (घमंडी, शेखीबाज़)
 
 
• **Example: **He was boastful about his wealth and success, which made others uncomfortable.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'modest' **is **'boastful'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Boastful**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Unimpressive **(अप्रभावी): Something that fails to impress or make a strong impact.

 
 
• **Example:** His performance in the play was unimpressive and lacked energy.
 
 
 
• **Moderate **(सामान्य, संतुलित): Average in amount, intensity, or degree; neither too much nor too little.
 
 
• **Example: **The weather today is moderate, neither too hot nor too cold.
 
 
 
• **Humble** (नम्र, विनम्र): Having or showing a modest or low estimation of one’s importance.
 
 
• **Example:** Despite his great achievements, he remains humble and kind.

questions.question:
Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the given idiom.

When pigs fly
questions.solution:

• **Example: **He’ll start being punctual when pigs fly.
 
 
 
• **"Just impossible"** refers to something that cannot happen, no matter the circumstances. (बस असंभव)
 
 
• **Example: **Winning the race without practice is just impossible.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the idiom "When pigs fly" expresses the same meaning as "Just impossible."

• **Example:** The team worked in unity to achieve their goals.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: In due course of time **(समय के साथ): Refers to something happening eventually or after some time.
 
 
• **Example:** In due course of time, he became an expert in his field.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Correct approach** (सही दृष्टिकोण): Refers to the right way or method to handle a situation.
 
 
• **Example:** Adopting a correct approach is key to resolving conflicts.

• **Sloth** (आलस्य): Reluctance to work or make an effort; laziness.

• **Generous** (उदार): Willing to give or share more than is usual or expected.
 
 
• **Example: **She is known for her generous donations to charity.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Cacophony
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Harmony**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Cacophony"** means a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds; it refers to noise that is unpleasant or jarring. (कर्कश ध्वनि)

 
 
• **Example:** The cacophony of car horns and shouting made it hard to concentrate.
 
 
 
• **"Harmony"** refers to a pleasing arrangement or combination of sounds, thoughts, or actions that are balanced and peaceful. (सामंजस्य)
 
 
• **Example:** The choir sang in perfect harmony, creating an enchanting melody.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Cacophony'** is **'Harmony'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Harmony**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Discord** (कलह): A lack of agreement or harmony, often leading to conflict.

 
 
• **Example:** There was discord among the team members over the project strategy.
 
 
 
• **Noise** (शोर): Unpleasant or unwanted sound that disrupts or annoys.
 
 
• **Example:** The noise from the construction site was unbearable.
 
 
 
• **Dissonance** (असंगति): A lack of harmony among musical notes or inconsistency in ideas.
 
 
• **Example:** The dissonance in their opinions made it difficult to reach a consensus.
